<thought>Using the ESI‑MS spectrum, the most intense ion appears at m/z ≈ 233.96. Assuming this is the [M+H]⁺ ion, the neutral monoisotopic mass is about 232.96 Da. The isotopic pattern shows a significant M+2 peak (~24 % of the base peak), consistent with the presence of a single chlorine atom. A molecular formula that matches the neutral mass and includes one chlorine atom is C₉H₁₀O₅Cl (exact monoisotopic mass ≈ 233.02 Da, which is within typical experimental tolerance). Therefore, the most plausible molecular formula is C9H10O5Cl.</thought>
<final_answer>C9H10O5Cl</final_answer>
